Check column-set/type compatibility for a set operation, dplyr-style

Source: R/sets.R
check_set_op_compatible.Rd

Mirrors dplyr:::is_compatible() (checked against dplyr 1.2.1 + vctrs vec_ptype2()): same column count, same column name set (order tolerated), and a per-column common type, via resolve_common_col_type() (R/bind.R), the same ladder bind_rows()'s own compute_unified_schema() uses. That ladder follows vctrs' vec_ptype2(), which refuses a numeric/date column against a character one (vec_ptype2(1L, "a") errors), so neither verb coerces such a pair to a string.

Usage

check_set_op_compatible(x_schema, y_schema)

Arguments

x_schema, y_schema

Schemas (current_schema()) of x/y.

Value

A list with $target_schema (unified schema, x's names/order), $needs_fallback (logical: TRUE for duplicated column names, or a Date next to a non-UTC POSIXct) and $fallback_reason.

Details

Factor columns get a four-way split (as vec_ptype2() treats factors, see inline comments): both-factor with identical levels runs on the GPU as is (same underlying INT32 codes, safe to compare/concatenate directly); both-factor with differing levels runs on the GPU through gpu_remap_codes() (src/ops_bind.cpp), which remaps each side's codes onto the level union, as bind_rows() does; factor-vs-character runs on the GPU through gpu_decode_factor(), which decodes the factor side to its labels, as bind_rows() does. Factor vs. anything else (numeric, date, ...) is a genuine vctrs error, reproduced here directly.

This function adds the column-count/name-set checks and its own verb-specific ("x and y are not compatible.", bulleted) error formatting on top of the shared ladder. A Date-vs-POSIXct column promotes to POSIXct on the GPU (gpu_cast_column()'s timestamp targets), except next to a non-UTC POSIXct, where the Date becomes local midnight of that zone: $needs_fallback is then TRUE, as it is for duplicated column names.
